verdict_reason: Only 2 of this pile's 28 photos were sampled to the contact sheet (2 tiles, 2 different photographers), so this verdict rests on a very thin sample. The one photo with real locational content is unambiguously the outdoor courtyard of the Vietnam Military History Museum on Dien Bien Phu street: a UH-1 marked 'U.S. AIR FORCE' on a concrete plinth, flanked by the museum's two-storey arcaded colonial block and by the rubble-stone citadel wall with a pierced concrete balustrade that is the base of the Hanoi Flag Tower. That is exactly the kind of subject the pin sits on, and the neighbouring pile at 105.8398,21.0327 shows the same courtyard from the Flag Tower terrace. The second tile is a framed museum exhibit with no visible room, building or caption, so it neither supports nor contradicts. Verdict genuine, but weak by construction - 26 of 28 photos were never seen.

photos.evidence: A Bell UH-1 helicopter with 'U.S. AIR FORCE' painted on the tail boom and a USAF star-and-bar roundel, mounted on a low concrete plinth with cast steps, in an open paved courtyard. To the left a two-storey cream French-colonial block with arched arcade openings and a balustraded first-floor balcony; to the right a rough rubble-stone wall topped by a pierced concrete balustrade, and tourists with bonsai pots along the yard. The captured-aircraft-on-plinth display plus that colonial block and citadel wall match the Military History Museum courtyard at the foot of the Hanoi Flag Tower; the same colonial block and balustrade appear in photo 5828971948 of the adjacent pile, shot from the Flag Tower terrace looking into this yard.

A framed, sun-faded American 'blood chit' escape-and-evasion flag: a US flag over the same appeal printed in English, Chinese, Lao, Thai, Khmer, Vietnamese, Burmese and other scripts, with a large enlarged Vietnamese-French-English transcription panel beside it. The frame stands against a dark rough surface with foliage reflected in the glass. There is no room, wall, building, exhibit label or bilingual museum caption in frame, so nothing fixes which museum or even which city; blood chits like this are shown in several Vietnamese war museums. I will not guess a place from a war exhibit alone.
